protocol.sample: 30 resolved CALLS per repo, fixed seed 42 (deterministic)
protocol.method: each sample checked by reading the source line and reasoning about the receiver's declared type from the surrounding source (imports, field/param declarations)

aggregate.confidence_of_wrong: all 7 wrong bindings are at heuristic confidences (0.75 unique-name or 0.98 same-file); ZERO wrong bindings at import_resolution 1.0 / qualified_name_resolution 0.99

root_cause: receiver type is not tracked by the L1 syntax-only resolver: any instance call whose short name matches exactly one in-project method (or one same-file method) binds at 0.75/0.98 regardless of the receiver's declared type. This is a KNOWN boundary of the frozen V0 ladder, language-wide (Python behaves identically), NOT a P1 regression (P1 guards type_usage/object_creation only).
implications: high-confidence resolved edges (1.0/0.99) remain safe for consumption as-is
heuristic-confidence edges (0.75/0.98) must be treated as Candidate (consistent with the platform-wide 'resolved != Verified' contract)
the JDT Phase 2 path (ADR) directly eliminates this class: type-flow-aware binding resolved all 4-5 of these shapes CORRECTLY in the T9-B fixture equivalents
no resolver contract change is made in this longrun (changing 0.75 semantics needs a dedicated design review; evidence recorded here feeds it)
